name: Plaza Mayor de Madrid

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/16657232 (centroid of the square's outline, way 4263036; heading = the Casa de la Panadería, north side, facing south into the square)

rights.note: Square built 1617–1619 by Juan Gómez de Mora on a plan going back to Juan de Herrera (Casa de la Panadería begun by Diego Sillero, 1590); rebuilt after the fires of 1631 (Gómez de Mora), 1672 (Tomás Román) and 1790 (Juan de Villanueva, who lowered the houses to three floors and closed the corners with the arches); works finished in 1854 under Antonio López Aguado and Custodio Moreno. Slate roofs replaced the Arab tiles in the 1960s. The murals of the Casa de la Panadería (Carlos Franco, 1992) are recent and are not reproduced: the model only gives that façade a warmer colour with abstract colour panels.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1123493_plaza_mayor_madrid.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. A ring around the square: the façade line, the corners and the tower notches come from the OSM outline of the square; the portico range is a uniform 6 m band (the open ground floor mapped in OSM) with lintelled granite porticoes, three floors of balconied windows in red-ochre plaster, granite string courses and pilaster strips, a granite cornice and a slate roof with dormers and an iron railing; the Casa de la Panadería (north, painted façade: warmer colour, abstract colour panels, central aedicule, gilt crown) and the Casa de la Carnicería (south) have round-arched arcades and two towers each with slate caps, clocks, lanterns and spires. Six large arches (Toledo, Gerona, Sal, Felipe III, Siete de Julio, Ciudad Rodrigo) rise through the first floor; Zaragoza, Botoneras and the Arco del Triunfo are plain openings at the back of the portico; the Arco de Cuchilleros is the passage over the stone steps at the south-west corner with its granite arch on Calle de Cuchilleros. Behind the range, the 27 OSM buildings that touch the square are extruded from their outlines (minus the band) to 16.4–17.4 m with flat tops, ochre/cream street façades with windows only where a wall faces a street; their real pitched tile roofs, courtyards, light wells and different heights are simplified. Uncertain: heights measured on photos (±5 %), the number and spacing of bays (3.2–3.7 m, not counted house by house), the size of the large arches, the ground level outside (foundations to −3 m, −9 to −12 m to the west and south-west where Cava de San Miguel and Calle de Cuchilleros lie lower). Main façade = the Panadería: +Z points south, so the default front view looks at the back of the south range. footprint is the ring of houses with a slit to the square (even-odd keyhole): the square, its paving and the statue of Felipe III are not cleared.
